## What you'll be able to do {#outcomes}

By the end of this lesson you will have:

- VS Code, git, R and Quarto installed on your computer.
- A GitHub account.
- Confirmed each one works, so the rest of the course runs smoothly.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Time:** ~30–60 min (one-off) · **You'll produce:** a working setup, checked with a few
version commands.
:::

## Why this matters {#why}

Every later lesson assumes these tools are ready. Doing the install once, carefully, now
means you never get stuck on environment problems in the middle of real work. You don't
need to understand the tools yet — just get them on your machine and confirm they run.

## What you need {#prerequisites}

- A computer you can install software on (administrator rights).
- About an hour, and a stable internet connection.

## Walkthrough {#walkthrough}

Install these four, in order. Each links to the official download — accept the default
options unless told otherwise.

1. **VS Code** — your editor and home base. Download from
   <https://code.visualstudio.com> and run the installer.
   - On Windows, tick **"Add to PATH"** if offered.
2. **git** — the version-control tool.
   - **Windows:** install **Git for Windows** from <https://git-scm.com/download/win>
     (accept defaults).
   - **macOS:** open the **Terminal** app and run `xcode-select --install`, or get git
     from <https://git-scm.com/download/mac>.
3. **R** — the language several lessons use. Download from <https://cran.r-project.org>
   and install the version for your operating system.
4. **Quarto** — turns your `.qmd` files into documents and websites. Download from
   <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/> and run the installer.

Then add two VS Code extensions (open VS Code, click the **Extensions** icon on the left,
search, and click **Install**):

- **Quarto** (by Posit) — preview and render documents.
- **R** (by REditorSupport) — work with R files.

::: {.callout-tip}
You can also install the **GitHub Copilot** extension now if your organisation provides
it — we'll use it later. It's optional for this lesson.
:::

Finally, create your **GitHub account** at <https://github.com> if you don't have one,
using your work email.

## Try it yourself {#try}

Confirm everything installed correctly. In VS Code, open a terminal
(**Terminal ▸ New Terminal**) and run these one at a time:

```bash
git --version
quarto --version
R --version
```

## Verify {#verify}

Each command should print a **version number** (for example, `git version 2.45.1`), not
an error like *"command not found"* or *"not recognised"*. If all three print versions,
your toolkit is ready.

If one fails, it's almost always because the program was installed but the terminal was
opened *before* the install finished — **close and reopen VS Code**, then try again.

## Common pitfalls {#pitfalls}

- **"Command not found" right after installing.** Close and reopen VS Code (or restart
  your computer) so it picks up the newly installed tools.
- **No admin rights.** If an installer is blocked, ask your IT team to install VS Code,
  git, R and Quarto for you — these are standard, safe tools.
- **Windows vs macOS.** Use the correct download for your system; the steps are otherwise
  the same.

## Recap {#recap}

You've installed the whole toolkit and confirmed it works. That one-off effort means the
rest of the course can focus on the actual synthesis workflow, not on setup.

## What's next {#next}

Next you'll **meet the agent** — the AI assistant you'll work with throughout — and learn
the one rule that keeps its help trustworthy.
